caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 532 of 1995.
lawyer:
Md. Awlad Ali, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md. Sajjadul Huq, Advocate-on-Record — For the Petitioners. 
Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record — For the Respondents.
parties:
Shahidur Rahman Majumder (Md), Md. Shahidullah Majumder and others  ----- Petitioners
vs.
Sabirunnessa & others  ----- Respondents.
full_judgment:
Md. Ismailuddin Sarker J : One Fakir Ahmed and Angia Khatun, petitioner No. 6 instituted a suit for partition being Title Suit No. 150 of 1964 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Comilla Sadar, against petitioner Nos. 1-5 and others and the suit was decreed in preliminary form on 13-6-1967. After the preliminary decree an Advocate Commissioner was appointed to effect partition of the suit property who submitted a report, according to which the final decree was passed on 10-11-1967; but the said final decree was set aside by the learned Assistant Judge on 26-1-1988 by exercising his inherent jurisdiction under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. Thereafter another Advocate Commissioner was appointed by the learned Assistant Judge on 16-4-1992 for effecting partition of the suit property in accordance with the preliminary decree and the Advocate Commissioner submitted his report on 29-11-1992 along with field book, map, etc. On receipt of the report of the Advocate Commissioner the Assistant Judge fixed 13.1.1992 for filing any objection against the Commissioner's report but since no objection has been filed by any party, the Commissioner's report was accepted by the learned Assistant Judge on 16-1-1993 and accordingly, final decree was passed on 19.1.1993 and the final decree was sealed and signed on 21-1-1993. Thereafter Title. Execution Case No. 1 of 1993 was filed by some of the parties in the proceeding for getting possession of their land allotted in their saham. Thereafter on 24.1.1993 defendants 8 (ka) and 8 (Cha) filed an application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for cancellation of the Advocate Commissioner's report, after setting aside the final decree on the ground that the sahams were not allotted according to the preliminary decree and the learned Assistant Judge after hearing the parties rejected the Advocate Commissioner's report by his order dated 22-2-1993 in exercise of his jurisdiction under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and thereby set aside the final decree. 

 3. It is contended by Mr. Md. Awlad Ali, learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners, that the learned Judge of the High Court Division has committed an error of law in not holding that the Advocate Commissioner's report was not in accordance with the preliminary decree and he has rendered the final decree ineffective and that the trial Court was right in setting aside the final decree in exercise of its power under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. There is no substance in the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioners, inasmuch as other remedies such as an appeal is provided by the Code of Civil Procedure; and when there is specific provision for appeal the Court cannot exercise its inherent power under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. This is not a case of clerical mistake which can be corrected by the trial Court under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure. As such, the learned Judge of the High Court Division rightly held that the learned Assistant Judge has committed an illegality in interfering with the final decree under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
